This always saves as the same filename, GraduateRegistry_Master.xlsx — so a linked table in Microsoft Access will pick up the latest export automatically after you hit Refresh All. This copy is not encrypted, so keep the Access folder itself access-controlled.

For a portable backup (USB drive, cloud folder, email), use Encrypted backup instead — it's protected with a password you choose, using AES-256 encryption. Files load back in only through Restore encrypted backup above, not by double-clicking in Windows/Excel. Anthropic/Claude never sees this password or the backup file — encryption happens entirely in your browser. There is no password recovery: if it's lost, the backup can't be opened.

05 Cloud Sync (Google Sheets)

Not connected

This mirrors your records to a Google Sheet in your own Google Drive as a real off-device backup. Since this file runs as a plain local file, Google requires a one-time setup before it will allow the connection — follow the steps below in order.

1

Host this file at a URL

Google's login screen refuses to work with a file opened straight from your computer (file://…). The free, easiest option is GitHub Pages: create a free GitHub account, make a new repository, upload this HTML file, then turn on Pages in the repo's Settings → Pages. You'll get a URL like https://yourname.github.io/repo-name/. Any other web host works too.

2

Create a Google Cloud OAuth Client ID

At console.cloud.google.com: create a project → enable the Google Sheets API and Google Drive API (APIs & Services → Library) → go to APIs & Services → Credentials → Create Credentials → OAuth client ID → type Web application → under "Authorized JavaScript origins" add the hosted URL from Step 1 (just the origin, e.g. https://yourname.github.io). Copy the Client ID it gives you.

3

Connect your Google account

Sign in and grant access to just the Sheets this app creates or opens — not your whole Drive.

4

Link a spreadsheet

Create a brand-new Google Sheet for this registry, or paste the URL/ID of an existing one.
